16. Equilibrium and Time

Two-period interest determination and overlapping generations — present-value budgets, credit market clearing, and the infinite-horizon warning.

  • Intertemporal Equilibrium and the Interest Rate — Trade period 1 for period 2 along the present-value budget line. At the market-clearing rate 1+r=E2/(δE1)1 + r = E_2/(\delta E_1)1+r=E2​/(δE1​), the period-1-rich consumer becomes the lender.
  • Overlapping Generations and the Golden Rule — Money links trades between generations that never meet. The monetary steady state and the golden rule (e/2,e/2)(e/2, e/2)(e/2,e/2) coincide only at δ=1\delta = 1δ=1 — with infinite horizons, the First Welfare Theorem's conclusion can fail.
